$comment: Why a word is in its case: the controlled list of functions used by case-lens markup [[form|lemma|case|function]]. A function may be used with its own case only (except "chunk").

functions.label: subject
functions.explain: The person or thing doing the action, or being described, is in the nominative: the dictionary form.

functions.label: naming: "to je…"
functions.explain: After to je / to jsou ("this is…") and after být with a noun describing the subject, the noun stays in the nominative.

functions.label: after z (from, out of)
functions.explain: Z ("from, out of") always takes the genitive. Jsem z Anglie: I am from England.

functions.label: after do (to, into)
functions.explain: Do ("to, into") takes the genitive: going into a building, a city or a country.

functions.label: after u (at, by)
functions.explain: U ("at, by, at someone's place") takes the genitive.

functions.label: after bez (without)
functions.explain: Bez ("without") takes the genitive.

functions.label: after od (from someone, since)
functions.explain: Od ("from" a person, "since") takes the genitive.

example.en: I have it from a colleague.

functions.label: of: whose
functions.explain: A noun that answers "whose? of what?" goes in the genitive, after the noun it belongs to.

functions.label: after 5 and more
functions.explain: After pět (5) and higher numbers, and after kolik, hodně, málo, the noun goes into the genitive plural.

functions.label: after 2, 3, 4
functions.explain: After dva/dvě, tři and čtyři, the noun is in the nominative plural.

functions.label: to whom: the recipient
functions.explain: The person you give, send, say or show something to is in the dative.

example.en: I'll give it to my colleague.

functions.label: who feels it
functions.explain: With feelings and states (je mi zima, líbí se mi, chutná mi) the person who feels it is in the dative.

functions.label: after k (towards, to someone's)
functions.explain: K / ke ("towards; to someone's place") takes the dative.

functions.label: direct object
functions.explain: The thing or person the action is done to (I want X, I have X, I see X) is in the accusative.

functions.label: after na: where to
functions.explain: Na with movement (where to?) takes the accusative: jdu na poštu.

example.en: I'm going to the post office.

functions.label: after pro (for)
functions.explain: Pro ("for") takes the accusative.

functions.label: after za (for, in exchange)
functions.explain: Za meaning "for (a price), in exchange for" takes the accusative. Díky za…, za sto korun.

functions.label: how long
functions.explain: A stretch of time with no preposition (celý den, každý týden) is in the accusative.

functions.label: addressing someone
functions.explain: When you call or speak to someone by name or title, the name changes into the vocative: Petr → Petře, paní Nováková stays.

functions.label: after v / na: where
functions.explain: V ("in") and na ("on, at") describing where something is (not where to) take the locative.

functions.label: after o (about)
functions.explain: O meaning "about" takes the locative: mluvit o práci.

functions.label: after po (after, around)
functions.explain: Po meaning "after" or "around/along" takes the locative.

functions.label: after s (with)
functions.explain: S / se ("with, together with") takes the instrumental.

functions.label: by means of
functions.explain: How you do something, including how you travel, goes in the instrumental with no preposition: jedu tramvají.

functions.label: after před, za, nad, pod, mezi: where
functions.explain: Před (in front of), za (behind), nad (above), pod (under) and mezi (between), describing where something is, take the instrumental.

example.en: I'm waiting in front of the station.

functions.label: fixed phrase
functions.explain: A fixed phrase learnt as a whole for now. The grammar behind it is taught later on the line.
